walkthroughs.body_html:
Organisms Respond to Changes — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Organisms Respond to Changes brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Organisms Respond to Changes.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.
Competition only happens between predators and their prey.

mcqs.q: Why is the cohesion-tension theory critical for water transport in plants?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.
Cohesion-tension describes how water diffuses freely between cells.
Hydrogen bonds between water molecules keep the water column unbroken under tension, so transpiration can pull water up from the roots.

mcqs.q: How do insulin and glucagon work together to regulate blood glucose?
options: They are antagonistic — insulin lowers blood glucose (cells take up glucose, store as glycogen); glucagon raises it (glycogen broken back down to glucose).
Insulin and glucagon both lower blood glucose using different mechanisms.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glycosidic bond”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polymer”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrolysis”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Condensation reaction”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monomer”?
options: Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
